key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer creates a synergistic Schottky solar cell that boosts both efficiency and environmental stability by combining charge transport, doping, anti-reflection, and moisture barrier functions.
engineering_relevance: This architecture shows a practical low-cost route to more durable silicon-based photovoltaic devices using ultrathin carbon and polymer layers instead of complex fabrication.
method: Built planar PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si and reference Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si cells on untextured substrates.
Benchmarked photovoltaic performance to separate the optoelectronic roles of graphene and PEDOT:PSS.
Evaluated long-term ambient stability over 75 days to test moisture resistance.
evidence_signal: The trilayer device reached 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for pristine Gr/n-Si and retained about 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days, while bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si retained only ~29%.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful interfacial engineering; the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS layer can still degrade without graphene protection, so encapsulation and process control remain important.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
